Check random fingerprick glucose:
If fingerprick glucose < 4 with/without symptoms 19.
If fingerprick glucose ≥ 11.1 with symptoms 19.
If fingerprick glucose ≥ 11.1 without symptoms, check urine dipstick for ketones. If ketones present 19. If no ketones, give routine diabetes care below:
DIABETES: ROUTINE CARE

1A TB contact refers to a patient who shared an enclosed space (at work, socially, in a hostel, or in a household setting), for ≥ 1 night or for frequent/extended daytime periods, with an adult/adolescent with pulmonary TB ("index patient"), during the 3-month period before the index patient started their TB treatment. 2One drink is 1 tot of spirits, or 1 small glass (125mL) of wine or 1 can/bottle (330mL) of beer. 3If eGFR < 60, repeat instead at 2 weeks.
Assess the patient with diabetes not needing urgent attention
Assess When to assess Note
Symptoms Every visit Ask about chest pain 24 and leg pain 80. Manage other symptoms as on symptom pages.
TB Every visit If cough, weight loss, night sweats or fever, test for TB 102. If TB contact1 100.
Mental health At diagnosis and if control poor If stress, anxiety or low mood 98.
Cancer risk Yearly Check for symptoms/signs suggestive of cancer or if eligible for cancer screening 194.
Substance use At diagnosis and if control poor In the past year, has patient drunk ≥ 4 drinks2/session, used drugs or misused prescription/over-the-counter medications? If yes to any 165.
Palliative care If advanced diabetes-related complications If any of: kidney failure, severe CVD, stroke, non-healing diabetic foot disease or recurrent severe emergencies 191.
BP Every visit If known hypertension 149. If not known hypertension and BP ≥ 140/90 148.
BMI, waist circumference (WC), waist-hip ratio (WHR)

• Weight: every visit • BMI, WC, WHR: at diagnosis, yearly • Aim for BMI 18 to < 25. If BMI ≥ 25, manage the overweight patient 156. • Aim for WC < 80cm if woman or < 94cm if man. Aim for a WHR < 0.85 if woman and < 0.90 if man.
Eyes At diagnosis, yearly and if visual problems Check visual acuity and fundoscopy. If visual problems, cataracts or retinopathy, refer.
Feet At diagnosis, yearly and more often if problems Check for pain, pulses, sensation, deformity, skin problems. For foot screen and foot care education 81.
Family planning Every visit Assess patient’s contraceptive needs 170. If pregnant or planning pregnancy, refer for specialist care.
Fingerprick glucose Every visit If fasting glucose > 8 or glucose taken 2 hours after eating > 10, step up treatment 147.
HbA1c (glucose control over past 3 months)
• Yearly • 3-6 monthly if treatment aim not reached or treatment change

• Aim for HbA1c < 7.0% for most patients; HbA1c < 6.5% if young/newly diagnosed/CVD risk < 10%/no known CVD; HbA1c < 7.5% if > 65 years, CVD risk > 10% or poor short-term prognosis. • If treatment aim not reached and adherent 147. If not adherent, give support 195 and repeat HbA1c after 3 months.

Urine dipstick At diagnosis and yearly • If protein, start enalapril if not already on it 147. • If no protein and not on enalapril, send urine to lab for albumin/creatinine ratio. If ratio > 3mg/mmol or > 30mg/g, start enalapril 147.

Creatinine (eGFR) • At diagnosis, then yearly • If eGFR 30-60 and on metformin: 3-6 monthly • If eGFR < 60, discuss with doctor. If known chronic kidney disease 155. • If eGFR < 30 stop metformin and glimepiride and discuss/refer same day.
Potassium If on enalapril/eGFR < 30: at diagnosis and yearly If starting enalapril: at baseline and after 4 weeks3
If potassium > 5.5, discuss/refer to doctor same day to assess whether to decrease/stop enalapril.
Lipids At diagnosis Check fasting total cholesterol, triglycerides, HDL/LDL. Assess CVD risk 142. If total cholesterol > 7.5 or triglycerides > 10, discuss/refer.
